ARCHIVE IS A ONE-WAY DOOR IN THIS CLI, so a janitor pass cannot undo its own mistake -- check for a LIVE INSTANCE before archiving a [persistent] rule. Measured this pass (run 0074 r2, lane `ajc-rr`).

## What happened
I archived `I-0362` and `I-0349` as "old, run 0048, superseded" on age and provenance. Re-reading them afterwards, both were wrong to archive: each is the single home of a rule with an OPEN instance at HEAD -- `I-0515` (nine advertised-but-absent declarations) for one, `I-0600` (the unrooted 41-file Ledger cone) for the other.

## Why it could not simply be undone
There is no `inbox unarchive`. `inbox archive` takes only an id, and `inbox edit` accepts only `--body` and `--kind` -- **not `--status`**. So an archive is irreversible through the documented interface, and the only repair is the `I-0482` route: re-file the content as a new item and comment the originals with a pointer. Done here as `I-0624`, consolidating both halves.

## The cost, which is not zero
The re-file spends a NEW id and loses the originals comment history (8 and 4 comments, including three prior consolidations). Net effect of the whole excursion: -2 items then +1, so -1 rather than the -2 the archive claimed. A janitor that archives on age will do this repeatedly.

## THE TEST, before archiving any rule-shaped memory
Grep the OPEN item set for an instance of the rule. If one exists, the rule is load-bearing today and the item stays -- however old it is. Age and run number are not evidence of staleness for a `[persistent]` rule; only the absence of live instances is.

Corollary for the arithmetic every janitor pass reports: an archive-then-refile shows up as a smaller reduction than the archive count suggests. Report the NET.

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StableAffineCover

/-!
# The `G`-stable affine cover for a bare finite group action

`Sym^n C` is a quotient of `C^n` by `S_n`, and the route to it that
`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6 identifies — explicit `Scheme.GlueData` from affine charts —
needs one geometric input above all others: **every point has an affine open neighbourhood
stable under the whole group**. Without it the charts cannot be chosen compatibly and the
quotient exists only as an algebraic space (the Hironaka trap recorded in
`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).

That input was believed missing for `S_n`. It is not: `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean` proves
it, sorry-free, and its proof **never uses the Galois structure it is stated over**.

## What was actually going on

`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`'s `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` is stated
for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — a group homomorphism `Gal(L/K) →* Aut X` *together with*
a field `compat`, the commuting square over `Spec γ` that makes the action semilinear. Reading
the proof, the only things it consumes are `ρ.act` and the two one-line consequences
`act_one_hom` / `act_mul_hom`, which are `map_one` and `map_mul` of the underlying
`MonoidHom`. `compat` — all of the semilinearity — is never mentioned, and
`[FiniteDimensional K L]` is spent only on getting a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`.

So the theorem is about a **finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms**; the Galois
data decorates the statement. This file states that version. It is a re-derivation, not a
generalisation of the original in place: `Picard/` belongs to another lane, so the proof is
copied here with the binder replaced (`G →* Aut X` plus `Fintype G`) rather than the original
being weakened. The two files should eventually be one, and the note below says which
direction that should go.

## Main results

* `StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis, for a bare action:
  every orbit lies in an affine open. Essential, not technical — see the Hironaka trap.
* `StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen` — a `G`-stable open.
* `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits` — **the theorem**: under that hypothesis every point
  has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood. Prime avoidance puts the orbit in a basic open
  `D(s)` inside `⋂_g g⁻¹U`, and the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)` cuts out a stable affine basic open.
* `permAction` — the `S_n`-action on a product, as the `MonoidHom` this file consumes, so the
  symmetric-power case can be fed in directly.

## Why the proof needs no averaging, and so no characteristic hypothesis

The norm `∏_g g(s)` is a *product*, not an average: it needs no `1/|G|` and works in every
characteristic. That matters here for the same reason it matters in
`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` — `g!` may vanish in `k̄` when `char k̄ ≤ g`, so any route
through averaging would exclude exactly the cases the challenge is stated over.

## Scope — what this does and does not give

**Does**: the stable-cover input to a glue-data construction, for `S_n` acting on `C^n`, with
no Galois hypothesis and no characteristic hypothesis.

**Does not**: build the glue data. `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` remains open, and
`AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are unchanged. Two further inputs a glue-data assembly needs
are also unaddressed here: that the affine chart quotients agree on overlaps (the cocycle
condition), and `OrbitsInAffineOpen` **for the curve** — which is where quasi-projectivity
would enter, and mathlib has no quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin. So this closes one
of three, and the remaining two are named rather than estimated.

Note also: nothing consumes this file yet. It is stated so the `S_n` case *can* consume it,
which is a different claim from having wired it in.

## References

Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94. EGA II 4.5.4 for the
orbit-in-affine hypothesis. The original proof is
`AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction.exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`
(`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean:193`), whose supporting lemmas
(`exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite`, `mem_finset_inf`, `preimage_finset_inf`,
`basicOpen_finset_prod`) are imported and reused unchanged.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace StableGroupAction

variable {G : Type u} [Group G] [Fintype G] {X : Scheme.{u}} (act : G →* Aut X)

/-- **Orbit-in-affine hypothesis for a bare action** (EGA II 4.5.4): every orbit is contained
in an affine open. This hypothesis is *essential*, not a convenience — without it the
quotient need only be an algebraic space (Hironaka; see `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`'s
module docstring). It holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no quasi-projectivity
at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by hand. -/
def OrbitsInAffineOpen : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ g : G, (act g).hom.base x ∈ U.1

/-- A `G`-stable open of `X`. -/
def IsStableOpen (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U

omit [Fintype G] in
/-- The identity acts as the identity. This and `act_mul_hom` are the *only* structural facts
the main theorem uses about the action — both are `map_one`/`map_mul` of the `MonoidHom`,
which is why no semilinearity is needed. -/
lemma act_one_hom : (act 1).hom = 𝟙 X := by rw [map_one]; rfl

omit [Fintype G] in
/-- Multiplicativity, in the composition order `Aut` gives. -/
lemma act_mul_hom (g t : G) : (act (g * t)).hom = (act t).hom ≫ (act g).hom := by
  rw [map_mul]; rfl

end StableGroupAction

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- **The `G`-stable affine neighbourhood theorem, for a bare finite group action.**

Under the orbit-in-affine hypothesis, every point has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood.

The argument, in three moves: prime avoidance (`exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite`) puts the whole
orbit of `x` inside a basic open `D(s)` contained in `W = ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹U`; the **norm**
`N = ∏_g g(s)|_W` then satisfies `D(N) = ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹ D(s)`, which is `G`-stable by
reindexing the intersection; and `D(N) ⊆ D(s) ⊆ U` is affine as a basic open of an affine.
Stability is proved at the level of *opens*, which is what avoids transporting sections along
the action isomorphisms.

The norm is a product, so no `1/|G|` appears and the statement is characteristic-free.

**Provenance.** This is `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean:193` with its `SemilinearGalAction`
binder replaced by `G →* Aut X` and `[Fintype G]`; the proof term is otherwise unchanged, which
is the evidence that the semilinearity field was never load-bearing. See the module header. -/
theorem exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits (h : OrbitsInAffineOpen act) (x : X) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ IsStableOpen act U := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨U, hxU⟩ := h x
  -- the whole orbit meets every translated chart: `g(t(x)) = (g*t)(x) ∈ U`.
  have horb : ∀ t g : G, (act g).hom.base ((act t).hom.base x) ∈ U.1 := by
    intro t g
    have hh : (act g).hom.base ((act t).hom.base x) = (act (g * t)).hom.base x := by
      rw [act_mul_hom act g t]; rfl
    rw [hh]; exact hxU (g * t)
  -- prime avoidance: `orbit ⊆ D(s) ⊆ W := ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹ U`.
  obtain ⟨s, hs_mem, hs_le⟩ := exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite U.2
    (fun g : G => (act g).hom.base x) hxU
    (V := Finset.univ.inf fun g : G => (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)
    (fun t => mem_finset_inf.mpr fun g _ => horb t g)
  have hWle : ∀ g : G,
      (Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) ≤ (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1 :=
    fun g => Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)
  -- the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)|_W` and its factors
  set t : G → Γ(X, Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :=
    fun g => X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle g)).op ((act g).hom.app U.1 s) with ht
  set N : Γ(X, Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) := ∏ g : G, t g with hN
  -- each factor cuts out the corresponding translate of `D(s)` inside `W`
  have hbo_t : ∀ g : G, X.basicOpen (t g) =
      (Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) ⊓ (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
    intro g
    rw [ht, Scheme.basicOpen_res, ← Scheme.preimage_basicOpen]
  -- the `g = 1` translate is `D(s)` itself
  have hP1 : (act (1 : G)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s = X.basicOpen s := by
    rw [act_one_hom act]; rfl
  -- `D(N) = ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹ D(s)`
  have hbo_N : X.basicOpen N = Finset.univ.inf fun g : G => (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
    rw [hN, basicOpen_finset_prod ⟨1, Finset.mem_univ 1⟩,
      Finset.inf_congr rfl fun g _ => hbo_t g]
    refine le_antisymm
      (Finset.le_inf fun g _ => (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)).trans inf_le_right)
      (Finset.le_inf fun g _ => le_inf (le_trans ?_ hs_le)
        (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)))
    exact le_of_le_of_eq (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ 1)) hP1
  -- `D(N) ⊆ D(s)` (the `g = 1` factor)
  have hNs : X.basicOpen N ≤ X.basicOpen s := by
    rw [hbo_N]
    exact le_of_le_of_eq (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ 1)) hP1
  refine ⟨X.basicOpen N, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- affineness: `D(N)` is a basic open of the affine `D(s)`
    have heq : X.basicOpen (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hs_le).op N) = X.basicOpen N := by
      rw [Scheme.basicOpen_res]
      exact inf_eq_right.mpr hNs
    rw [← heq]
    exact (U.2.basicOpen s).basicOpen _
  · -- membership: prime avoidance put the whole orbit in `D(s)`
    rw [hbo_N, mem_finset_inf]
    intro g _
    change (act g).hom.base x ∈ X.basicOpen s
    exact hs_mem g
  · -- stability, at the level of opens: preimage functoriality plus reindexing
    intro tau
    rw [hbo_N, preimage_finset_inf]
    have hPt : ∀ g : G, (act tau).hom ⁻¹ᵁ ((act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s)
        = (act (g * tau)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
      intro g
      rw [act_mul_hom act]; rfl
    rw [Finset.inf_congr rfl fun g _ => hPt g]
    refine le_antisymm (Finset.le_inf fun d _ => ?_) (Finset.le_inf fun d _ => ?_)
    · have hh := Finset.inf_le (s := Finset.univ)
        (f := fun g : G => (act (g * tau)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s)
        (Finset.mem_univ (d * tau⁻¹))
      rwa [inv_mul_cancel_right] at hh
    · exact Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ (d * tau))

end StableGroupAction

---
name: statement-decoration-vs-proof
description: A theorem's binder can carry structure its proof never touches; grep the body for the structure's PROJECTIONS, and the "missing" lemma may already exist under a richer statement.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A walled input can already be proved under a **richer statement whose extra structure the
proof never uses**. The test is cheap and mechanical: grep the theorem body for the
*projections* of the structure in its binder. If the load-bearing field never appears, the
statement is decoration.

AJC run 0069 r5 (ajc-albanese). `Sym^g C`'s gluing needed "every point has a `G`-stable
affine open neighbourhood" for `G = S_n` finite. That was priced as missing. It existed:
`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean:193`, sorry-free — but stated for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f`
of `Gal(L/K)`, so it read as Galois-descent machinery, not as what I needed.

Grepping the body (lines 193-272) for `ρ.*` returned exactly `ρ.act`, `act_one_hom`,
`act_mul_hom`, `IsStableOpen`, `OrbitsInAffineOpen`. The structure's `compat` field — *all* of
the semilinearity, the commuting square over `Spec γ` — never appears; `act_one_hom` and
`act_mul_hom` are `map_one`/`map_mul` of the underlying `MonoidHom`. `[FiniteDimensional K L]`
buys only a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`. Verdict: the proof is about a finite group acting on a
scheme by automorphisms.

**Confirmed by kernel, not by reading**: copied the body verbatim with the binder replaced by
`(act : G →* Aut X)` + `[Fintype G]`. Compiled with zero errors — only two
`omit [Fintype G]` linter notes on the two helper lemmas.

**Why to apply:** this is the mirror of [[measure-absence-at-the-root]] and
[[gate-inferred-from-absent-name]]. Those say an absence claim can be scoped to the wrong
*cone* or inferred from a missing *name*. This one: the claim can be defeated by a statement
that is strictly *stronger* than what you need, because a search for your hypotheses will not
match it. Related: [[obligation-stated-too-strongly]] is the same phenomenon on the obligation
side, and [[availability-is-cone-relative]] on the reachability side.

**How to apply:** when a geometric input looks missing, search for the *conclusion* rather than
the hypotheses, then for each near-miss grep the proof body for the projections of whatever
structure decorates its binder. If the interesting field is absent, restate with a bare binder
and re-run — the proof term usually ports unchanged. Do NOT weaken the original in place if it
belongs to another lane; re-derive under your own path and say so in the docstring.

One measurement worth reusing: the norm trick (`∏_g g(s)`) that makes the stable open is a
*product*, not an average, so it needs no `1/|G|` and holds in every characteristic — which is
what makes it usable at `char k̄ ≤ g`, exactly where averaging routes die. See
[[sym-g-as-interface-not-sorry]] for the surrounding leg.

---
name: unstateable-vs-unproved
description: Milne's (A^⊗n)^{S_n} was not unproved but UNSTATEABLE — mathlib had the permutation only as a linear equiv, so FixedPoints.subring could not be applied; also the letI-with-implicit-index trap.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Distinguish **unproved** from **unstateable**. A carrier can be absent from a tree not because
nobody proved a theorem about it but because its *type* cannot be written down, and that
diagnosis changes the fix from "prove something" to "supply one instance".

AJC run 0069 r5 (ajc-albanese). Milne III.3.1's affine carrier `(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` was recorded
for several sessions as an open specialisation. The real situation: mathlib has the `CommRing`
and `R`-algebra structure on `⨂[R] i, A i` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PiTensorProduct.lean`) but
factor permutation only as a **linear** equiv (`PiTensorProduct.reindex`) — there is no
`reindexAlgEquiv`. So `MulSemiringAction (Equiv.Perm ι)` on the tensor power does not
synthesize, and `FixedPoints.subring` *requires* that instance. The invariant subring of a
tensor power could not be stated at all.

Fix, small: `liftAlgHom` applied to `(tprod R).domDomCongr e`. Unitality and multiplicativity
are pointwise on tuples, so no side conditions. Landed as `Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean`
(4097b4b5a), with the `Under k` layer in `Albanese/SymPowInvariantsUnder.lean` (0f0559696).

Four traps worth keeping:

1. `permAlgHom` is an **anti**-homomorphism: `comp d e = permAlgHom (e * d)`. So the action
   must send `σ ↦ permAlgHom σ⁻¹`. Same inversion appears three times in this cone (here,
   `SymPowColimit.permEnd` for `End`'s `f * g = g ≫ f`, and the `Groupoid.invEquivalence`
   reindexing) — consistency, not error.
2. `FixedPoints.subALGEBRA` additionally needs `[SMulCommClass G R B]`, also absent. Either
   supply it (one `map_smul`, since `permAlgHom` is an algebra hom) or state the carrier with
   `permAlgHom` directly so its *type* mentions no action instance.
3. **`letI` of an action whose index type is implicit leaves a metavariable.**
   `letI := permMulSemiringAction R A` inside a *statement* gives
   "typeclass instance problem is stuck: HSMul ...". Always name it: `(ι := ι)`.
4. With the action supplied by `letI`, goals display as `σ • x = x`, not in terms of
   `permAlgHom` — so `Eq.symm` of the `permAlgHom` form is a type mismatch. Introduce the
   group element and apply directly.

**Why:** [[cannot-be-constructed-is-a-probe]] warns that a "no such thing exists" verdict is
often about pinned values rather than totality. This is the complementary case where the
verdict was right but *misfiled*: the blocker was one missing instance, not a theorem. Related:
[[sym-g-as-interface-not-sorry]], [[tensor-side-conditions-are-keying]] (also a
"missing infrastructure" record that was really instance keying).

**How to apply:** before pricing a carrier as open work, try to *write its type*. If the type
does not elaborate, the gap is an instance and is usually hours, not sessions.
